name: Berechiah
overview: Berechiah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Shimea. He belonged to the Gershonite branch, descendants of Gershon, son of Levi, which highlights his role within the Levitical family responsible for specific religious duties. His lineage situates him within the priestly tribe, emphasizing his connection to the worship and service of God.
namesAndTitles: The name Berechiah means 'y-h-v-h blesses,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the LORD. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:39, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but reveals a recognition of divine blessing associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Berechiah as the son of Shimea. It is also inferred that he was the father of Asaph, linking him to a significant Levitical family line. Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Berechiah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogy, particularly among the Gershonites, which underscores his role in the service and worship of God. His connection as the son of Shimea and probable father of Asaph situates him within a lineage important to the musical and liturgical traditions of Israel. This lineage contributes to the continuity of Levitical duties and the preservation of worship practices under the Old Testament covenant.
